name: WiseLending empty-pool share inflation through a direct WBTC donation
summary: WiseLending v1 credited any token surplus in a pool to existing shares (_cleanUp) and minted one share per wei into an empty pool. The attacker made two one-wei WBTC deposits, donated flash-loaned WBTC so each share was worth a fortune, borrowed every other asset against that collateral, and pulled the WBTC back through rounding-favoured withdrawals.
notes: The age runs from the owner's createPool for WBTC (collateral factor and pool data): the empty WBTC market was the collateral the exploit inflated, and it was the latest listing before the exploit; the runtime itself is immutable.

The coffeebabe searcher executed the anchor and returned part of its take to Wise, but most of the proceeds went to the block builder and proposer, so it is an unaffiliated exploit. The later copycat drained the WBTC dust the anchor left, net of its own deposit.
aEthWETH is valued at the ETH price (Aave v3 aTokens redeem one for one); stablecoins at DefiLlama or par. Recoveries are not subtracted.
